subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equations of the tangents to the circle x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 12 = 0 and parallel to the line x + y − 8 = 0.

mark_split.label: Parallel line and the touching condition

insider_note: Any line parallel to x + y − 8 = 0 is x + y + k = 0 — keeping the same coefficients and changing only the constant is the whole idea, and the answer is a pair because k has two values.

steps.label: Centre and radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. The constant is negative, so −c adds and the radius is a whole number.
steps.memory_tip: Centre (−g, −f) and radius √(g² + f² − c). Here −c is +12.
steps.why: The touching condition compares the distance of a line from the centre with the radius, so both are needed before any line is written down.

steps.label: Parallel line and the touching condition
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Keep the coefficients 1 and 1 and change only the constant; that is what "parallel" means here.
steps.memory_tip: Parallel to x + y − 8 = 0 means x + y + k = 0. Only k changes.
lines: Any line parallel to x + y − 8 = 0 is x + y + k = 0
If it touches the circle then p = r
steps.why: Two lines are parallel when they have the same coefficients of x and y, so only the constant is unknown. The modulus gives two values of k, which is right, because a circle has two tangents of any given slope.
common_mistakes: Writing the parallel line as x + y − 8 + k = 0, which double-counts the constant.
Dropping the modulus and finding only one value of k.

steps.label: The two tangents
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Both values of k must appear; the ± form is accepted and is shorter to write.
steps.memory_tip: Put k = 1 ± 5√2 back into x + y + k = 0.
lines: Substituting k = 1 ± 5√2 in x + y + k = 0:
steps.why: The two lines are the same distance from the centre, one on each side, which is why their constants are 1 + 5√2 and 1 − 5√2 — placed symmetrically about the value 1 that would put the line through the centre.
common_mistakes: Giving only the tangent with the plus sign.

steps.label: The picture
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own; the question does not ask for a diagram. The book prints one showing the given line outside the circle.
steps.memory_tip: The given line is only a direction. Slide it either way until it touches, and there are two positions.

elements.text: slide the given line until it touches

steps.why: The given line sets the direction only. Moving a line of that direction towards the circle, it touches once on the near side and once on the far side, and those two positions are the two tangents.
common_mistakes: Treating the given line itself as one of the tangents.
Drawing the two tangents with different slopes.
